Palatable

/PAL-uh-tuh-buhl/ - the stress falls on PAL · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Palatable means pleasant or acceptable to taste.

Dad's first curries were merely palatable; by December the family had stopped keeping a backup pizza in the freezer.

Worked Example

The wilderness course saves one lesson for the last night: the instructors serve boiled cattail root, plain. It is, everyone agrees, palatable — you can eat it, nobody gags, a hungry hiker finishes the bowl. No one asks for seconds. Then the instructors add butter and salt from their packs and serve it again, and the lesson lands: survival food and supper are two ingredients apart.

Palatable is the quietest praise food can earn: it clears the bar of pleasantness and stops climbing. Below it sits edible — safe, and that is all; above it, delicious. The word also moonlights outside the kitchen: a palatable plan or palatable truth is one people can swallow — the mouth's ruling, borrowed by the mind.

How Palatable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tasty

tasty: plain, warm praise

appetizing

appetizing: invites the first bite — as much about look and smell as taste

Antonyms

unappetizing

unappetizing: kills the appetite before the fork moves

foul

foul: actively revolting

How Strong Is It? — edible → palatable → delicious

edible vs. palatable

edible vs. palatable: Edible promises only that you can safely swallow it; palatable promises you won't mind doing so.

delicious vs. palatable

delicious vs. palatable: Delicious outruns palatable by a mile: palatable food is eaten without complaint, delicious food is eaten without leftovers.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — palat

Root — palat: the palate — the roof of the mouth, the seat of taste

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: agreeable to

Put it together

Put it together: Palat (the palate, the roof of the mouth and old headquarters of taste) + -able = agreeable to the palate. Note the suffix moonlighting: here -able means 'suitable to, agreeable to' rather than 'able to be' — the same handy hinge as in fashionable. Anatomists no longer credit the palate with tasting, but the word keeps the older map of the mouth.

Use the root in a new word: palate

Use the root in a new word: palate: Years of tasting trained the judge's palate to find one sour grape in a sweet harvest.

Word Choice

neutral / faint praise

Palatable is the quietest of food praise — pleasant enough, no seconds requested — and it moonlights for ideas: a palatable plan is one people can swallow. Its unit-mate potable answers a different question entirely: palatable asks 'is it pleasant?', potable asks 'is it safe to drink?'
